# Step 5: Slots

## Introduction

Describe what you can say about each class: its color, its maker, the foods it pairs with.

A class with no description is just a name. [Slots](../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-slot) are how an ontology holds facts. They also keep the model tidy, because you attach each slot to one class and every class below it gets it for free ([inheritance](../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-inheritance)). You can read the full guide to this step in [Methodology](../../../docs/METHOD.md#step-5-slots).

## What you'll make

11 slots. Some hold a value, like `color` or `body`. Others link to another thing, like `maker`. You'll attach each slot to the most general class that can use it.

## Run the commands

A [slot](../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-slot) comes in two kinds. A **property** holds a value, such as `light` or `Napa Valley`. A **relationship** links to another thing, such as a winery. okb stores a relationship as an edge in the graph.

Start with the properties every wine has. The `--values` list is the allowed set, and `--card single` sets the [cardinality](../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-cardinality), which is how many values the slot can hold. Here it's one at most:

```bash
okb property add color --on Wine --type Enumerated --values red,white,rose --card single --desc "The wine's color."
okb property add body --on Wine --type Enumerated --values light,medium,full --card single --desc "How heavy the wine feels in the mouth."
okb property add flavor --on Wine --type Enumerated --values delicate,moderate,strong --card single --desc "Intensity of the wine's flavor."
okb property add sugar --on Wine --type Enumerated --values dry,offDry,sweet --card single --desc "Residual sweetness."
```

```text
Added property color on Wine (Enumerated).

Added property body on Wine (Enumerated).

Added property flavor on Wine (Enumerated).

Added property sugar on Wine (Enumerated).
```

Tannin comes from grape skins, so only red wines have it. Attach it to RedWine, not Wine:

```bash
okb property add tanninLevel --on RedWine --type Enumerated --values low,moderate,high --card single --desc "Astringency from grape skins; only meaningful for red wines."
```

```text
Added property tanninLevel on RedWine (Enumerated).
```

Now add the links between things. `--min 1` means a wine must have at least one maker:

```bash
okb relationship add maker --from Wine --to Winery --card single --min 1 --desc "The winery that produced the wine."
okb relationship add produces --from Winery --to Wine --card multiple --desc "Wines the winery makes."
okb relationship add grape --from Wine --to WineGrape --card multiple --min 1 --desc "Grape varieties the wine is made from."
okb relationship add region --from Wine --to WineRegion --card single --desc "Where the wine comes from."
okb property add location --on Winery --type String --card single --desc "Where the winery is."
okb relationship add goesWellWith --from Wine --to Food --card multiple --desc "Foods this wine pairs well with."
```

```text
Added relationship maker: (Wine)-[:MAKER]->(Winery).

Added relationship produces: (Winery)-[:PRODUCES]->(Wine).

Added relationship grape: (Wine)-[:GRAPE]->(WineGrape).

Added relationship region: (Wine)-[:REGION]->(WineRegion).

Added property location on Winery (String).

Added relationship goesWellWith: (Wine)-[:GOES_WELL_WITH]->(Food).
```

Then look at what RedWine ended up with:

```bash
okb show RedWine
```

```text
RedWine  Class · c.red-wine
  Wine made from dark-skinned grapes with skin contact; described by tannin level.
  parents        Wine
  subclasses     Bordeaux, Beaujolais, Merlot, Port
  disjoint with  WhiteWine, RoseWine

  Slots  (properties hold values; relationships → link to other things)
    tanninLevel        Enumerated, {low, moderate, high}, single
    color              Enumerated, {red, white, rose}, single (from Wine)
    body               Enumerated, {light, medium, full}, single (from Wine)
    flavor             Enumerated, {delicate, moderate, strong}, single (from Wine)
    sugar              Enumerated, {dry, offDry, sweet}, single (from Wine)
    maker              Instance, → Winery (:MAKER), single, min 1 (from Wine)
    grape              Instance, → WineGrape (:GRAPE), multiple, min 1 (from Wine)
    region             Instance, → WineRegion (:REGION), single (from Wine)
    goesWellWith       Instance, → Food (:GOES_WELL_WITH), multiple (from Wine)
```

## Read the output

- **[Inheritance](../../../docs/learn/slot-inheritance.md).** RedWine lists `color`, `body`, `flavor` and `sugar` "from Wine". You added them once, and every class below RedWine [inherits](../../../docs/GLOSSARY.md#concept-inheritance) them too.
- **Tannin stays on RedWine.** Only red wines show `tanninLevel`. A white wine can't be given one by mistake.
- **[Properties versus relationships](../../../docs/learn/properties-and-relationships.md).** `maker` shows `→ Winery (:MAKER)`. The `:MAKER` is the name of the edge okb will store. `body` has no arrow, because it holds a plain value.
- **Two slots for one fact.** `maker` and `produces` are the same fact seen from each side. Step 6 joins them.

When step 5 has a tick, move on:

```bash

```

```text
Now on step 6. (To read a step's guide without moving: okb explain 6)

Step 6 of 8: Define the facets of the slots

  Goal: For every slot, decide its value type, allowed values or range, cardinality, and any
  defaults, fixed values or inverse.
  Why it matters: Facets turn a list of fields into rules a machine can check. This is where
  most data-quality errors get caught later.

Questions to answer
  • Is the value text, a number, yes/no, one of a fixed list, or another thing (Instance)?
  • If it's a fixed list, what are all the allowed values?
  • If it's another thing, what is the most general class of things it can be (the range)? Not
  too general, not too narrow.
  • One value or many? Is it required (minimum 1)?
  • Is there a value most instances share (default), or one every instance of a class must have
  (fixed value)?
  • Is this relationship the reverse of another slot (maker ↔ produces)?
  • Does each link need extra information of its own, like a condition or a strength? (Edge
  properties; see decision.edge-or-class.)

You're done when
  ○ Every slot has a value type and cardinality
  ○ The slots have no known mistakes

Tips
  • When in doubt about range, pick the most general class that still only contains valid
  fillers.
  • Defaults are suggestions; fixed values are facts. Don't confuse them.

In Ontology 101's wine example
  • body: one of light, medium or full, and only one value
  • produces (on Winery): points to Wine, can have many values, and is the inverse of maker
  • grape: at least one value
  • Dessert Wine: sugar is fixed at sweet

Decision guides for this step  (okb explain <id>)
  decision.range               What should this slot's range be?
  decision.edge-or-class       Edge property, or make the relationship its own class?

Commands
  okb slot set   okb relationship inverse   okb relationship property   okb class fix   okb class default   okb class restrict
```

> **Common mistakes**
>
> - **Attaching a slot too high.** If `tanninLevel` were on Wine, every white wine would be asked for one.
> - **Attaching a slot too low.** If `color` were on each of the four color classes, you'd repeat yourself and drift apart later.
> - **Using a property for a thing.** If the value is something with its own details, like a winery, make it a relationship.

## Next step

You added 11 slots: properties that hold values, and relationships that link one thing to another. Next, you'll add limits and shortcuts, such as fixed values and inverses.
